---
title: "Linking"
---

A `codNota` is a concept of the gazette, and the Court's snapshots know nothing
of it. `nota2md.linking` is the one place in the project that knows how a
snapshot becomes a `codNota`: it matches every snapshot of a law against the
DOF's own titles, and `legal_provisions`' SCJN path resolves the other
direction, a `codNota` back to the snapshot it produced, through the same
module. Nothing on the SCJN side imports it; `scjn` depends on no sibling
package, and the seam sits here.

## How a snapshot gets its `codNota`

For every snapshot of a law, dated by the SCJN's own reform table, the linking
looks at the DOF's notes of that same day (the titles stream of the
`notas-archivo` release) and asks two questions in order.

1. **Does a same-day title name the instrument?** The candidates are the notes
   whose own title explicitly names the law (`title_candidates`); when no title
   does, whichever same-day note opens with "DECRETO" or "LEY" is taken, since a
   reform's title does not always spell out every law it amends. A single
   candidate is the link.
2. **Which candidate's text explains the change?** Every entry also gets a
   content-diff confirmation: among that day's candidates with digital DOF text,
   the one whose own text best accounts for what actually changed between this
   snapshot and the previous one (`content_diff_confirmed_codNota`,
   `content_diff_score`). When the title alone could not pick a winner, the
   confirmation is the link, provided it clears the confirmation threshold and
   the candidate is not already claimed by another snapshot.

Each snapshot's `indice.json` entry records the `codNota` matched to it
(`null` when none), every same-day candidate, how the pool was resolved
(`title_link_status`: `linked`, `content_diff`, `none`, `claimed` or
`ambiguous`) and its confirmation. The DOF notes considered while linking
travel inside each law's own tarball, so a link can be audited without going
back to the network.

An absent link is worth more than a wrong one: a date left `ambiguous`, several
same-day candidates and no content confirmation among them, is reported for a
human to review, never guessed. As of the release, 3,291 of the 3,724 `leyes`
snapshots are linked to a `codNota`, 2,474 by title alone and 834 more by their
content-diff confirmation; 526 of the linked ones are pre-1999.

## What a `codNota` is used for

- `legal_provisions(codNota)` consults the reverse index
  (`download_scjn_leyes_index`) to decide whether the note is covered at all,
  and reads the snapshot it maps to.
- `reconstruct_legal_provisions` takes a law's `codNota` list, which
  `download_scjn_leyes_corpus` gives one entry per reform, oldest first.
- "Reform N" of a law is the position of the reform in the SCJN's own
  chronological reform table, and a law's reform history is the `scjn-leyes`
  release itself: `nota2md` publishes no dataset of its own.

## The script

`scripts/enlaza_scjn_legislacion.py` runs the linking over a crawl workspace,
one `indice.json` per law, and is step 4 of `scjn`'s crawl process. See
[Scripts](scripts.qmd).
